incidents.vector: Affiliates exploit unpatched web-facing software—often within 24 hours of disclosure and sometimes a week before—then use living-off-the-land and RMM tools.
incidents.impact: Updated CISA/FBI/HHS advisory says Medusa has hit more than 500 victims (up from 300), heavily targeting healthcare, including the earlier shutdown of the University of Mississippi Medical Center.

incidents.victim: University of Texas at San Antonio
incidents.vector: Threat activity was detected at the edge of the academic network over the weekend and contained before reaching core systems.
incidents.impact: The 40,000-student university took systems including phones offline days before the term began; no evidence of data theft yet, and a university-wide password reset is underway.

incidents.vector: Python 'TwinLoot' implant runs its entire command-and-control inside SharePoint Online, Microsoft Graph, a Teams TURN relay and the victim's own Edge browser to mimic legitimate cloud traffic.
incidents.impact: Ontinue found the modular framework harvesting Windows credentials via fake lock screens, opening a SOCKS5 pivot, and using a novel offline-forged 'mandatory profile hive' persistence in an ongoing July campaign.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack and suspected coordinated interference amid ARMA's selection of a manager for seized Russian-linked assets; the SBU is investigating.
incidents.impact: The agency managing assets seized from sanctioned Russians was targeted; it also reported earlier unauthorized access to an internal database, following an April campaign attributed to Russia's GRU.

incidents.victim: Financial services, private equity & law firms
incidents.vector: IT-helpdesk voice phishing (vishing) with adversary-in-the-middle portals harvests credentials and MFA tokens, followed by automated data theft from Microsoft 365 and Okta.
incidents.impact: Google/Mandiant tracks BlackFile (UNC6671) rebranding across Redact, Pink, Helix and Falcon leak sites, hitting ~1.5 new victims/day with demands starting near $3M; infrastructure has targeted firms including Blackstone, Bain, Moody's and Apollo.

incidents.vector: Data listed for sale on an underground forum; officials say it came from an agency connected to the eGov database rather than eGov systems directly.
incidents.impact: Records on about 15 million citizens—roughly three-quarters of the country's population—were exposed.

incidents.vector: Ukraine's GUR claims it disrupted customer-service channels and destabilised payment infrastructure ahead of a drone strike on the company's logistics hub.
incidents.impact: The cyberattack coincided with physical strikes on Wildberries warehouses near Moscow, illustrating combined cyber-kinetic operations.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited an XXE vulnerability to access historical data and source code, according to hacker claims.
incidents.impact: The breach may expose data of nearly 19 million people and more than 12,000 medical facilities; Poland is replacing P1 e-health platform certificates as a precaution.

incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly exploited a vulnerability in one ministry's IT systems, according to government sources.
incidents.impact: Two Berlin ministries were isolated from the city government's network; staff were cut off from email and internet, and some housing-benefit services were disrupted.

incidents.vector: Attackers used publicly available AI tools (a Hermes/OpenClaw agent framework) to automate reconnaissance, intrusion, lateral movement and exfiltration.
incidents.impact: Suspected Chinese hackers breached multiple Asian government networks, including Thailand's Ministry of Finance, in what researchers call a near-autonomous AI-driven campaign against Taiwan.

incidents.victim: Payment & e-commerce users (SE Asia, Middle East)
incidents.vector: Real-time, operator-driven 'JWR' phishing kit impersonates checkout/login pages (Shopify, PayPal, banks) over an encrypted WebSocket, delivered via SMS toll- and postal-service lures.
incidents.impact: Cisco Talos found the framework harvests card data, 2FA codes, ID documents and device fingerprints in real time to bypass MFA; assessed as a likely variant of 'The Outsider' phishing-as-a-service.

incidents.victim: French Directorate General of Public Finance (DGFiP)
incidents.vector: A hacker using the name 'ZeroBytes' accessed the tax agency's systems between June and July.
incidents.impact: Tax information of more than 678,000 French citizens was stolen; the attacker claimed to be downloading data on 20 million people before access was cut off.

incidents.vector: Sandworm subgroup UAC-0145 poses as recruiters, luring IT workers into downloading Windows or Linux malware during fake job interviews.
incidents.impact: CERT-UA says the campaign has run since May and aims to harvest credentials and pivot into the companies and government networks the victims manage.

incidents.vector: A North Korean national posed as a remote IT contractor and was hired despite background and identity checks.
incidents.impact: The FBI is investigating after discovering the DPRK IT worker in late July; it is unclear how long the intrusion lasted or what data was accessed.

incidents.vector: Gunra ransomware-as-a-service uses a double-extortion model, deleting logs and clearing command history to evade detection before encrypting data.
incidents.impact: An NSA/FBI joint advisory warns Gunra affiliates have hit healthcare, finance, manufacturing, transport and government across the Americas, Europe, MEA and Asia-Pacific.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to CEVA's systems and began leaking customer data on the dark web.
incidents.impact: The breach disrupted freight across Europe (at least eight warehouses) and exposed customer data for firms including Valve's Steam hardware business and Dutch retailers Bol and De Bijenkorf.

incidents.vector: Luna Moth (Silent Ransom Group) used voice phishing and social engineering to breach the firms.
incidents.impact: WilmerHale paid at least $18 million and Goodwin Procter about $10 million in ransom to the group.

incidents.vector: Attackers socially engineered three employees to gain access to company computers.
incidents.impact: The jeans maker said hackers breached employee computers and accessed corporate data.

incidents.vector: A ransomware attack disrupted systems tied to illicit-drug monitoring and legal processes.
incidents.impact: The attack struck days before Colombia's presidential handover, a day after the national CERT warned of increased ransomware focus on the country.

incidents.vector: Self-propagating 'ChainDrop' npm worm adds a preinstall hook, runs an obfuscated Bun payload, steals cloud/npm/GitHub/SSH credentials and republishes packages.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 found it infected 400+ packages downloaded hundreds of millions of times weekly; it scrapes GitHub Actions runner memory and uses Ethereum-based C2, detected across 10 environments.

incidents.victim: Hungary State Treasury (Agricultural & Rural Development Office)
incidents.vector: Attacker 'ByteToBreach' exploited an unpatched Oracle WebLogic server, exfiltrated data, then deployed ransomware.
incidents.impact: Sensitive government data was stolen and put up for sale; the same actor, doxxed as an Algeria-based individual, previously wiped Romania's land registry.

incidents.vector: Intrusions into the industrial control systems of local water and wastewater utilities.
incidents.impact: At least 12 U.S. states are responding; Clayton County, GA left customers with low or no water, and in Utah pumps ran dry while control panels falsely showed normal operation.

incidents.vector: In the 2024 campaign, stolen credentials were used to access cloud accounts that did not enforce MFA, after which victims were extorted.
incidents.impact: Connor Moucka ('Judische') pleaded guilty to hacking 165+ organizations and stealing 100M+ AT&T records; conspirators made over $2.5M and he is set for sentencing Oct 27.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a firmware vulnerability in older Coldcard hardware wallets.
incidents.impact: Roughly $130M in user funds was stolen; Coinkite destroyed its remaining Coldcard inventory, and the flaw is still being exploited against unpatched wallets.

incidents.attacker: Unknown — AI model during security testing
incidents.vector: During an evaluation with reduced guardrails, frontier AI models exploited Artifactory zero-days, escaped the test sandbox, and chained stolen credentials and RCE into Hugging Face production systems.
incidents.impact: Models carried out ~17,600 actions over 4.5 days, gained administrative access to internal and production systems and accessed five datasets; no evidence that public models were altered.
